newsitem.title: USA: US refiners revel in arb crude, June buying wanes.
newsitem.headline: US refiners revel in arb crude, June buying wanes.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast refiners revelled in a surge of North Sea Brent crude on Friday as June buying began to wind down, traders said.
A U.S. company sold three cargoes of Brent for around June 22-27 delivery over the past two days for some 80 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
At least two trading houses were showing Brent cargoes into the Gulf Coast around WTI minus 80-90 cents a barrel.

The sales reflect the continued wide spread between WTI and Brent. The July level was running around $1.75 a barrel Friday afternoon, down around five cents from Thursday but still wide enough to spur transatlantic activity.
Dated Brent was thinly talked at a steady July Brent minus 15-20 cents a barrel in Europe, traders said.
One trader attributed the wide arbitrage to speculative buying with little or no fundamental support. "There's a lot of speculative length entering the market," the trader said.
From West Africa, a European company on Thursday sold around 940,000 barrels of Bonny Light to a U.S. refiner for an undisclosed price related to WTI/Cushing.
Traders speculated that at least one company would deliver the Nigerian grade into the NYMEX upon expiry of the June contract next Tuesday.
Some of the foreign barrels were expected to be redeliveries of Bonny Light that were not absorbed when they were initially delivered into the NYMEX upon the May contract expiry last month.
But an additional 500,000 to one million fresh barrels of Bonny Light might also be delivered thanks to the wide arbitrage, traders said.

The premium paid to sellers of Bonny Light delivering Bonny Light into the NYMEX drops from 60 cents a barrel to 40 cents in the July contract, boosting the incentive for delivery next week, traders said.
The May contract expiry witnessed the delivery of 2.73 million barrels of Brent, Oseberg and Bonny Light out of total record deliveries of 6.621 million barrels.
In Latin America, Venezuela's Mesa-30 crude was offered around $3.20 under WTI/Cushing, with bids running around $3.50 discount, traders said.
Separately, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol today planned to award a tender for Vasconia crude loading around June 23-30.

Meanwhile, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP will seek to buy one million barrels of crude oil for delivery at the end of July in a formal tender to be announced probably next week, trade sources said.
The company normally seeks to purchase crude with an API gravity of 26-45 degrees and a sulfur content of 0.5 percent to 1.8 percent.
